knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = param, eval= param, include=T)

```{r setup-randomization, include=FALSE}
required_pkgs <- c("randomizr", "carat")
missing_pkgs <- required_pkgs[!vapply(required_pkgs, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]

if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "Please install the following packages before running this exercise: ",
      paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", ")
    )
  )
}

imbalance_summary <- function(trt, covariates) {
  tab_trt <- table(trt)
  cov_diffs <- lapply(names(covariates), function(v) {
    levs <- unique(covariates[[v]])
    s <- sapply(levs, function(lev) {
      abs(sum(trt == names(tab_trt)[1] & covariates[[v]] == lev) -
            sum(trt == names(tab_trt)[2] & covariates[[v]] == lev))
    })
    data.frame(variable = v, level = levs, abs_diff = as.numeric(s))
  })
  do.call(rbind, cov_diffs)
}

sum_covariate_imbalance <- function(trt, covariates) {
  tmp <- aggregate(
    abs_diff ~ variable,
    data = imbalance_summary(trt, covariates),
    sum
  )
  sum(tmp$abs_diff)
}
```

# Exercise - Minimization

Consider a trial with `n = 30` patients. For each patient, the variables `sex`, `age`, and `severity` are recorded before treatment allocation.

## Exercise 1

Simulate a dataset with these three variables. Then apply minimization with `carat::PocSimMIN()` and `p = 0.80` to allocate the patients to treatment `A` or `B`.


```{r}
set.seed(301)
n <- 30
covariates <- data.frame(
  sex = factor(sample(c("Female", "Male"), n, replace = TRUE)),
  age = factor(sample(c("Young", "Old"), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.55, 0.45))),
  severity = factor(sample(c("Low", "High"), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.60, 0.40)))
)

set.seed(302)
res.min <- carat::PocSimMIN(data = covariates, p = 0.80)
trt.min <- as.character(res.min$assignments)

trial.min <- cbind(covariates, treatment = trt.min)
head(trial.min, 10)
table(trial.min$treatment)
```


## Exercise 2

Using the same covariate dataset, also generate a treatment allocation with simple randomization using `randomizr::simple_ra()`. Compare the treatment counts and the covariate balance obtained under both methods.


```{r}
set.seed(303)
trt.simple <- randomizr::simple_ra(N = n, conditions = c("A", "B"))

table(trt.simple)
table(trt.min)

bal.simple <- aggregate(abs_diff ~ variable,
                        data = imbalance_summary(trt.simple, covariates),
                        sum)
bal.min <- aggregate(abs_diff ~ variable,
                     data = imbalance_summary(trt.min, covariates),
                     sum)

bal.simple
bal.min
```


## Exercise 3

Repeat the minimization procedure with `p = 0.60`, `p = 0.80`, and `p = 0.95`. Which value gives the strongest balance? Which value would make the procedure more predictable?



```{r}
set.seed(304)

p.values <- c(0.60, 0.80, 0.95)
nsim <- 200

res.p <- sapply(p.values, function(p) {

  mean(replicate(nsim, {

    trt <- as.character(
      carat::PocSimMIN(data = covariates, p = p)$assignments
    )

    sum_covariate_imbalance(trt, covariates)

  }))

})

res.p

comparison <- data.frame(
  p = p.values,
  mean_total_imbalance = as.numeric(res.p)
)

comparison

comparison[which.min(comparison$mean_total_imbalance), ]



```
